ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a ball is tied with a thin string and placed on a smooth inclined plane with an inclination angle of θ. During the process in which the thin string slowly shifts upward from the horizontal direction, how does the tension in the thin string change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, it can be seen that a ball is placed on an inclined plane sloping upward to the right, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is marked as θ; the ball is in contact with the inclined plane. On the right side of the ball, several dashed lines are drawn from near the ball toward the right, indicating that the position of the thin string gradually deflects upward from close to the horizontal direction. Then reason: Let the angle between the thin string and the horizontal direction be α. The ball moves slowly on the smooth inclined plane, and it can be analyzed according to static equilibrium at each position. The ball is subject to gravity mg, the support force N of the inclined plane on the ball, and the tension T of the thin string. Decompose the forces along the direction of the inclined plane; the support force has no component along the inclined plane; the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ; the component of the tension upward along the inclined plane is T cos(α-θ). The equilibrium condition is T cos(α-θ)=mg sinθ, so T=mg sinθ/cos(α-θ). When α gradually increases from 0, α first gradually approaches θ, cos(α-θ) increases, and T decreases; after α exceeds θ, cos(α-θ) decreases again, and T increases. Therefore, the tension in the thin string first decreases and then increases.
